run.question:
Our US prod cluster is having a checkout incident — investigate using
app-262-prod-logs.

report.summary: The only evidence of the checkout incident is in the app-262-prod-logs index, and it belongs to cluster production-us-east-1: checkout-service logged "POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)" at 2026-11-21T03:59:56Z, payment-service logged "Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms" at 04:59:56Z, and checkout-service logged "Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)" at 05:29:56Z. The same index's only production-eu-west-1 line is a checkout-service INFO "Healthy: success rate 99.7%" / "Healthy: p95 latency 230ms" at those same timestamps, so the failure is not visible outside the US cluster. The reachable Kubernetes cluster (node opspilot-m1-control-plane) contains only app-101 and otel-demo; it has no app-262 namespace and no region label, and its own checkout/payment workloads run the otel-demo mock payment service (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment), whose logs show repeated successful charges and no stripe, timeout or circuit-breaker lines — so it cannot be tied to production-us-east-1 and is not evidence of impact there. Prometheus and Jaeger both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE throughout this Run, so error rates, latencies and trace call edges for checkout-service/payment-service were not checked, and the external provider stripe-us is not observable in any available source. The deepest supported finding is therefore that payment-service's outbound 30s call to stripe-us failed and checkout-service then tripped its circuit breaker for payment-service; whether payment-service itself or the upstream provider is at fault remains unresolved, and no Kubernetes object was observed applying the fault, so no root cause object is named.

claims.text: The app-262-prod-logs index holds exactly 5 documents in the authorized window 2026-11-20T06:00:04Z–2026-11-21T06:00:04Z, spanning 2026-11-21T03:59:56Z to 05:29:56Z, and each document carries a `cluster` field whose values are production-us-east-1 and production-eu-west-1 (fields: cluster, level, message, service, timestamp).
In cluster production-us-east-1, service checkout-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-21T03:59:56Z: "POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)".
In cluster production-us-east-1, service payment-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-21T04:59:56Z: "Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms".

In cluster production-us-east-1, service checkout-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-21T05:29:56Z: "Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)"; that 44% figure is text from the log line, not a value computed from any metric or from these logs.

In cluster production-eu-west-1, service checkout-service logged INFO "Healthy: p95 latency 230ms" at 2026-11-21T04:59:56Z and INFO "Healthy: success rate 99.7%" at 2026-11-21T05:29:56Z — the only checkout-service lines for that cluster in the window report healthy operation at the same times the US cluster reports timeouts and an open circuit breaker.

The reachable Kubernetes cluster has namespaces app-101, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo — there is no app-262 namespace — and its single node is opspilot-m1-control-plane with no topology.kubernetes.io/region or failure-domain region label, so the reachable cluster cannot be identified as production-us-east-1 and holds no objects for the failing checkout-service/payment-service.

In the reachable cluster's otel-demo namespace, all 25 Deployments report readyReplicas equal to replicas (including checkout 1/1 image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout and payment 1/1 image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment), and all 34 pods across all namespaces are phase Running with containers ready; the checkout pod is checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n and the payment pod is payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, each owned by a ReplicaSet with restartCount 1.

The otel-demo checkout pod's own logs from 2026-11-21T05:03:48Z to 05:59:50Z contain continuous successful charges ("payment went through (transaction_id: ...)") and no line matching error/fail/timeout/circuit in 208 scanned lines, and the otel-demo payment pod's own logs show "Charge request received." followed by "Transaction complete." for each request with no stripe, timeout or error lines in 208 lines — this payment service is an in-cluster mock charge service, not the stripe-us-calling payment-service of production-us-east-1.

Feature-flag fault injection in otel-demo (paymentFailure / paymentUnreachable) as the cause was considered and rejected for the reachable cluster: in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) both flags are state ENABLED with defaultVariant "off" (all flags off), and that cluster's payment pod completed every charge in the window — this says nothing about the flag state of production-us-east-1, which I could not read.

Primary hypothesis: the upstream payment provider stripe-us did not answer /v1/charges within payment-service's 30s client timeout, so payment-service calls failed or hung, and checkout-service's circuit breaker for payment-service opened at a 44% failure rate — the three production-us-east-1 ERROR lines are consistent with this single chain, but the ERROR text alone does not distinguish a provider fault from a network or payment-service-side fault.

Competing hypothesis that remains open: payment-service in production-us-east-1 was itself degraded (saturation, upstream connection pool or its own latency) so that its outbound stripe-us calls exceeded 30s; without payment-service metrics or traces this cannot be separated from a stripe-us-side failure.

Once Prometheus is reachable, quantify the deviation for the exact service names in the US cluster — traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout-service"} and {service_name="payment-service"} by status_code, and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count / rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket by rpc_service, rpc_method and rpc_grpc_status_code over 2026-11-21T03:00Z–06:00Z — to establish when the error signal began and to separate payment-service-side latency from provider-side timeout.

Obtain Kubernetes access to production-us-east-1 and review the checkout-service and payment-service deployments/pods (status, container last termination reason and exit code, events) together with their logs, and review the checkout circuit-breaker thresholds and the 30s client timeout against the provider's observed latency.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for the whole Run: get_label_values, get_metric_names, metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query and list_prometheus_rules all returned status error / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error rate, latency, restart or saturation series (for example traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, kube_deployment_status_replicas_*) were read for checkout-service or payment-service; those signals are unchecked, not healthy.

Jaeger was unavailable: traces_list_services and traces_search for service checkout returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no trace spans, durations or parent references exist for this Run and the checkout->payment->stripe-us call edges are inferred only from log text, not from parent-child span references.

No Kubernetes objects for the failing systems could be read: the only reachable cluster is the kind cluster whose node is opspilot-m1-control-plane with namespaces app-101/otel-demo and no region label, and it has no app-262 namespace, so pod status, container last termination reasons, events and pod logs for checkout-service and payment-service in production-us-east-1 are unknown; nothing proves those workloads are or are not running.

The upstream dependency stripe-us is an external payment provider with no data source in this Run; its latency, error rate, availability and status for /v1/charges around 2026-11-21T03:59:56Z–05:29:56Z are unobserved, and I did not see the declared failure occur at its side.

The change_history integration is not available, so whether a deploy, config change, secret rotation or provider-side configuration change preceded 2026-11-21T03:59:56Z in production-us-east-1 is unknown; secrets (for example payment credentials or stripe-us keys) cannot be read and were not verified.

Log coverage is sparse: app-262-prod-logs contains only 5 documents in the 24-hour window, so the 44% failure rate, the number of failed checkouts and the start/end of the incident cannot be derived from logs and no counts or rates are claimed from them.

Two changes in the reachable cluster remain unplaced: Deployment app-101/loki scaled replica set loki-66445c6d6f from 0 to 1 at 2026-11-21T05:59:51Z (SuccessfulCreate, pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started), and a Warning event at 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z reported "Failed to create endpoint for service app-282/loki: endpoints 'loki' already exists"; no evidence ties either to the checkout errors, the app-282 namespace is not visible in this cluster, and the cause of the loki scaling is unknown.

Pod app-101/payment-api-101-8486559b69-tht28 (containers payment-api python:3.9-slim and promtail) is Running with 0 restarts but has no ReplicaSet among the listed ReplicaSets and wrote no log lines inside the window (8 promtail lines fell after the window end), so whether it is a log-shipping component or an application payment API, and whether it relates to checkout, is unknown.
next_steps: Restore or grant access to the Prometheus target and query the US-cluster error/latency series listed above for checkout-service and payment-service, comparing the pre-03:59Z baseline with the 03:59Z–05:30Z period before asserting any latency or error-rate trend.
Restore or grant access to Jaeger and pull full traces for failing checkout requests in production-us-east-1 to confirm the checkout->payment->stripe-us edge from parent references.

Request Kubernetes read access to the production-us-east-1 cluster and audit the checkout-service and payment-service workloads, their pods' last termination reasons/exit codes, events and logs, plus any fault-injection or chaos configuration in that cluster.

Ask the payments/provider owner for stripe-us /v1/charges latency and error data for 2026-11-21T03:30Z–06:00Z, and review whether the 30s client timeout and the checkout circuit-breaker thresholds are appropriate.
Review deployment and configuration change history for production-us-east-1 before 2026-11-21T03:59:56Z (change_history integration was not available in this Run).
